entry.name: Clock
entry.summary: A clock in the right rail, signed by its author.

plugins.description: A clock that shows the time or the ISO timestamp, and remembers which you picked.
plugins.readme:
Clock is the worked example of the third-party publishing path: a manifest, one script, one panel, and a package signed with the author's own release key.

Click the line under the time to switch between the local time and an ISO timestamp. The choice is stored in the plugin's own data directory.

entry.name: Todo
entry.summary: A task list in the right rail: priorities, search, inline editing and progress, kept between runs.

plugins.description:
A task list you can keep in the right rail. Each task carries a priority and the time it was added; the header shows how much of the list is done. Long lists scroll under the composer, and anything finished folds into a Done section that stays out of the way.

Type to add, click a row to rename it, click the bar to cycle its priority. Search appears once the list is longer than a few tasks, and the footer switches between All / Active / Done and Manual / Priority / Recent ordering. Everything is stored in the plugin's own data directory, so it survives a restart and a disable/enable cycle.
plugins.readme:
Todo is the smallest useful plugin, taken seriously: one panel, one list, one file.

**Adding.** Type in the field at the top and press Enter or click Add. The three chips under it set the priority the next task gets.

**Working the list.** Click a checkbox to finish a task; the header's bar and counter follow along. Click a row's text to rename it in place — Enter saves, Escape and an empty field cancel, so a slip of the keyboard cannot delete a task. The small bar on the left of each row is its priority; the `!` button cycles it.

**Finding things.** Past a few tasks a search field appears and filters as you type. The footer's All / Active / Done buttons filter, and the Manual / Priority / Recent buttons reorder.

**Finishing up.** Completed tasks fold into a Done section you can collapse with a click; Clear removes them. The choice of filter, ordering and whether Done is open are remembered too.

It asks for `ui.panel` (a place in the right rail) and `storage` (a file of its own), and nothing else.
